description:
Staff identity with roles (box office / admin / finance), the event & inventory builder UI, order management console (lookup, refund, exchange, resend, holds).

**Conditions of Success:**
- Role matrix enforced server-side; box-office staff cannot touch settlement
- Organizer builds a sellable event end-to-end in the UI without API calls
- Console handles the full order lifecycle staff-side

Lineage: docs/product/brief.md · docs/product/prd-v1.md (capability map).

comments.body: COS defined at epic level. Not yet decomposed — US-stories are created when the owner prioritizes this epic (Gate 1), per PRD 'Capability map'.

<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=summary -->
**Scope anchor (owner decision 2026-07-14):** this epic owns the organizer-facing **catalog builder UI** — the screens to author events, series, seasons, festivals and the typed dated-slot kinds (performance / festival_day / operating_day) plus their publish/archive lifecycle — over the catalog API built in **TKT-2** (children TKT-49…TKT-53). TKT-2 deliberately ships API + storefront only ("creation via API only", per the TKT-26 precedent); the builder UI and the staff identity/RBAC it sits behind are consolidated here so the organizer never touches curl. Decomposing TKT-22 must therefore depend on the relevant TKT-2 catalog endpoints being stable, and cover series/season/festival/slot authoring — not just the M1 single-GA-event shape.

<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=readiness -->
### ✅ Implementation readiness — CONCERNS

Decomposed into five vertical slices, chained by dependency:

| Child | Slice | Blocked by |
|---|---|---|
| TKT-184 | US-B1: Staff sign-in — a session gates the back office | — |
| TKT-185 | US-B2: The role matrix — box office cannot touch settlement | TKT-184 |
| TKT-186 | US-B3: Event builder — publish a sellable event without curl | TKT-185 |
| TKT-187 | US-B4: Order console — find an order, read its lifecycle | TKT-185 |
| TKT-188 | US-B5: Order console actions — refund and resend | TKT-187 |

| Criterion | Status | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Quality gates extracted | ✅ | `make check`, contract tests, **browser-submit** for every UI story, ADR-004 tier per read |
| Vertical slices | ✅ | Each child crosses schema→backend→UI→tests and is demoable alone |
| Prefactoring split out first | ✅ | US-B1 *is* the prefactor: the principal every later child gates on |
| Ordered by dependency | ✅ | No forward dependency; B3 and B4 are siblings off B2 and may run in either order |
| AC verifiable | ✅ | Every COS names an observable outcome; no "works correctly" |
| Links + cycle check | ✅ | Chain is a tree rooted at B1 — walked transitively, no cycle |
| Context-mémo per child | ✅ | `governingAdrs` resolved against `docs/adr/` at HEAD; every cited file verified present |
| No unvalidated assumption | ⚠️ | See concern 1 |

**Concerns:**
1. **TKT-184 — where staff identity lives is undecided.** ADR-002 cuts the system at five services plus a gateway, and the gateway owns no database today. The two candidates (a gateway-owned staff store enforcing at the edge, vs. a sixth `identity` service) are a real architecture decision, not a coding detail. It is carried as `approach: deferred` with an ADR as an explicit US-B1 deliverable, rather than pre-decided here.
2. **TKT-184 — a session cookie arrives while `checkOrigin` is disabled.** `web/backoffice/astro.config.mjs` sets `security.checkOrigin:false`, justified in TKT-105 by "the gateway is the trust boundary … no auth yet". US-B1 removes that premise, so its CSRF posture must be stated and enforced (`SameSite`), not inherited.
3. **TKT-188 — the console will surface known-open gaps.** A failed compensation refund has no automated path forward (TKT-144) and no operator unpark path (TKT-146); refunded tickets still admit at an OFFLINE gate (TKT-162). US-B5 must not render success or finality over any of those. Scoped by COS, not fixed here.
4. **No browser/e2e harness exists in-repo.** The browser-submit gate is real (TKT-105) but manual, and this epic is four UI stories. Each story carries the cost; expect the verification evidence to say precisely how the submit was driven.

**Verdict:** CONCERNS — proceedable. The decomposition is sound and dependency-clean; the named risks are design decisions deliberately routed to the plan gate (1, 2) and pre-existing platform gaps the children are scoped to respect rather than paper over (3, 4).
